temporal.meaning: Each period is the first day of the calendar year the observation describes, from the provider's Time column. The grain is one row per period and location_id. Stocks are measured on 1 July of that year and flows are totals over it. The panel is rectangular: every location carries every year from 1950 to 2100. Years up to the snapshot's represented date are the provider's estimates and later years are its medium-scenario projection, which series_kind records; a consumer that treats the two as one continuous observed series will read a model as a measurement. The provider's own 1 January row for the year after the projection horizon is excluded, because it carries a population stock and none of this table's flows or rates. Natural change and net migration do not sum exactly to population change in the provider's own figures: the residual is a few people for most country-years but reaches roughly 4,900 people for a country and 7,300 for the world aggregate, so the two components account for the change rather than decomposing it, and a consumer that stacks them will not close the total.

validations.description: There is exactly one observation for each location and calendar year.
validations.name: one-row-per-location-and-year

validations.description: Period, location identity, kind markers and population are never null.
validations.name: required-identity-and-population

validations.description: The provider's world aggregate is published for every year the table covers.
validations.name: the-world-total-is-present-in-every-year

validations.description: Every country or area carries an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, and only the world total does not.
validations.name: only-the-world-total-lacks-an-iso3-code

validations.description: Every location carries the same set of years, so a consumer reaching any year finds every location.
validations.name: the-panel-is-rectangular

validations.description: The provider's natural change equals its births minus its deaths, to the precision it publishes.
validations.name: natural-change-is-births-minus-deaths

validations.description: Every location's estimated years precede all of its projected years, and both are present.
validations.name: the-estimate-boundary-splits-the-series-once

validations.description: Populations and counts are non-negative, life expectancies and fertility rates lie in ranges a human population can take, and only migration and natural change may be negative.
validations.name: measures-lie-in-their-published-ranges
